messages:
deploy-bot: rollout started: sdk-client v2.3.1 -> staged 10% on production-us-east-1
Alice M.: getting paged, streaming endpoints spiking 502s, started triage
Ben R.: seeing repeated cursor decode failures in logs, looks like header mismatch between client and server v2 framing
Clare S.: confirmed, errors look like `invalid_frame_header: expected 0x7e, got 0x3a` from node-pool-7 and node-pool-8
Derek V.: timeline? which service pushed v2.3.1?
Alice M.: release started ~4102005540 per deploy dashboard, traffic ramp to 10% at 4102005555
Eva K.: customer impact: A subset of streaming SDK users on long-poll cursor flows are getting disconnects, estimated 3-6% of requests to /stream/paging are failing
Ben R.: paste of sample log: ```
2026-03-17T21:06:12.345Z node-7 stream ERROR cursor.decode failed invalid_frame_header expected=0x7e got=0x3a ctx={client_version:2.3.1}
2026-03-17T21:06:12.346Z node-7 stream WARN reconnecting client_id=aa3f
```
Clare S.: hypothesis: client bumped default framing for cursor tokens in v2.3.1 but server runtime expects legacy header for streaming paging. Decoder rejects leading byte and fails early
Derek V.: impact severity? customers seeing lost messages or only transient disconnects?
Alice M.: customer reports show dropped streams, some retries succeed, but for longer sessions stateful cursor resumes fail and cause user-facing errors in a couple of enterprise integrations
incident-bot: incident created INC-2026-0317-17: "staged rollout streaming cursor failures" assigned to oncall-eng
Alice M.: proposing mitigation: 1) flip FF to disable sdk-client v2.3.1 routing (kill staged rollout), 2) roll back client routing to v2.2.x for staged traffic, 3) notify customers and open support cases for affected integrations
Ben R.: quick check: can we accept both header formats in decoder with a compat flag? That would be lower-risk than full rollback if it's a single-byte header change
Clare S.: making a hotfix PR for permissive header sniffing, but it needs canary and deploy — we should avoid more rollout while we assess
Derek V.: execute kill-switch on rollout now, please. I'll coordinate rollback if that doesn't stop errors.
Alice M.: kill-switch issued: feature-flag `sdk_v2_3_routing` -> OFF at 4102005601 :white_check_mark:
Ben R.: monitoring… error rate on /stream/paging dropped from 5.2% -> 0.9% in last 30s, nodes warming down staging routing
Eva K.: customer impact update: support triage notes: 6 total customers affected, 2 enterprise customers reported failures, product teams notified to prepare incident comms
Derek V.: agree wait ~3 mins after FF kill to confirm. If still >1% errors, we initiate rollback of the canary artifacts and revert release manifest
Clare S.: permissive-decoder PR status: ready for review but requires runtime restart to pick up change. I'd prefer we roll back the client rollout and then ship the decoder patch in a controlled release
Alice M.: last check at 4102005685: error rate at 0.6% and trending down, latency unchanged. No new customer escalations in last 5m
incident-bot: INC-2026-0317-17 status -> mitigated (kill-switch) by Alice M.
Alice M.: next steps: 1) full rollback of v2.3.1 canary artifacts from CDN and client distribution (release team) 2) postmortem to capture root cause (protocol header change slipped past integration tests) 3) notify affected customers with timeline and remediation plan 4) add a gating e2e for streaming cursor compatibility in release pipeline
Ben R.: add task for decoder permissive-accept and strict-mode toggle so we can enable compatibility while tracking new header usage in telemetry
Eva K.: I will draft customer-facing note and open six support tickets to track impact and remediation per customer
Derek V.: handing incident to postmortem owner Clare S. for root cause and long-term fixes. Oncall shift handed off at 4102005699
Clare S.: acknowledged, I'll own the postmortem and coordinate with release and QA. Thanks team. :thanks:
